ethPandaOps would like to bring up the topic of how we proceed now that holesky has finalized: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/post-finality-path-forward-holesky

TLDR: With the large exit queue, holesky is not suitable for a lot of testing. We propose 4 potential paths forward and would like to choose the one that staking providers and the community would feel is most useful for them.

> ethPandaOps would like to bring up the topic of how we proceed now that holesky has finalized: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/post-finality-path-forward-holesky
> 
> TLDR: With the large exit queue, holesky is not suitable for a lot of testing. We propose 4 potential paths forward and would like to choose the one that staking providers and the community would feel is most useful for them.

I will not be able to attend the meeting, however here is my view of the path forward for holesky:

*A*: this is my preferred option, with a tweak.  When we launched sepolia and holesky there were various views on the lifetime of the testnet, however given what we have seen with holesky I believe that we should create a new testnet with a lower lifetime (max 3 years, ideally 2 years).  The rationale behind launching a new testnet, and launching one with a lower lifetime, is the same: too many contracts on, and tooling for, holesky are deployed/built and then forgotten without generating a repeatable process.  By keeping the idea that another deployment of the contracts and tooling is likely to happen for the person doing the initial work they are more likely to lay out processes to redeploy.  Even if people stick with the 5 year lifespan, this remains my preferred option as it results in a clean testnet (and although it's good for us to have gone through a recovery of holesky, we don't need to deal with the resultant scarring the other options that keep holesky alive will leave for the next 3 years).

*B*: this is a good network for those that need to test ASAP, as it is available right now.  As per my previous comment, turning deployments into a repeatable process is time well spent.  The difference in chain parameters should not matter, as long as the parameters are read from spec rather than hard-coded (and if they are this would help flush out the code that did that, making it more resilient).

*C*: this doesn't seem to have any significant benefits over other solutions, and seems to be a half-way house with some items (contract addresses) staying the same and others (genesis validators root?  fork version?) potentially changing.

*D*: not sure how this would work, likely a hard fork purely for holesky?  Possible, but it will probably take a while to code and test fully, and there's always a chance of it in turn going wrong.  Optics of that would be... bad.

Something for the agenda: we would like to propose JSON-RPC error code `4444` for the condition when an API call accesses pruned history. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/636 

We kind of pre-agreed this with people from Nethermind & Reth at the Portal Network Summit, but would be nice to get a formal decision in.

> ethPandaOps would like to bring up the topic of how we proceed now that holesky has finalized: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/post-finality-path-forward-holesky

Would like to share some feedback here on these options collected from discussions with some Lido contributors (and Node Operators and other staking infra/protocols). Our primary need is a fully working staking testnet with expected long-term longevity basically, and quite soon.

In the case of Lido, Holesky is the "main" testnet (almost like a testnet+QA environment rather than a sandbox), and I think for most other staking protocols too. If we can't test full lifecycle stuff, new features, etc. it's a huge cost to run it, and it is cost and operational workload prohibitive to run two "full" testnets (let's say both Holesky and the new testnet) indefinitely.

In the event of Option A, this means we'd probably have to "deprecate" the Lido testnet on Holesky. We could still use it until the testnet from Option A is up and running and we've deployed everything, and then slowly deprecate Holesky (by deprecate mean that we really can't keep all the infra running for 1.5 years, because it's not just us, but ~hundred node operators as well, oracle operators, incurring real costs etc.).

With that in mind, I think Option D is potentially the quickest thing that gets everyone there (but obviously runs the risk of creating more issues and as you say is not indicative of a real fix). Option A is the cleanest. We're ok with a plan like D+A where we give D an effort and a new staking-testnet also gets brought up and then we assess later where the "main" lido testnet would live (if that's operationally viable/sustainable).

If we go with Option A only then we'd probably have to fully transition from Holesky to the new testnet as the de-facto Lido testnet. The rest of the options unfortunately don't adequately address the primary need. Personally I think either the 5y lifetime view or 3y are ok. 

Estimated timelines in case of Option A:
3-4 days for "light" deploy, and ~1-2 months to have a full deployment with various UIs and full suite of governance functionality + sizeable set of independent node operators + oracles. 

A sufficient deployment to test Pectra substantively improved from current testing we did (on devnet) would be like the HF being 1-2 weeks after we've gotten deployed so we have at least some node operators and at least some 3rd party oracles set up

As a staking operator, we also use Holesky as our primary testnet. I agree with @isidorosp's suggestion, Option A brings stability in the long term. it would require a full transition from our current setup to the new one, including our testing platform.

With option A, might be good to start it before the Pectra fork so we can go through it again for validation purposes.

EthStaker is generally in favor of option A with a focus on lego deployment automation. If you are actively using a testnet with smart contracts, tools or interfaces for others to use, you should strongly consider automating your deployment process and documenting it so that your team or anyone else can easily and quickly redeploy it as needed.

I won't be able to make the meeting tonight but some summary points I guess.

It sounds like what we actually have in sepolia and holesky (or whatever its replaced with maybe) is 2 pre-production deployments which are basically production environments that should ideally never be broken in real terms due to the use-cases they represent.

We need something similar to these pre-prod environments that may get broken safely IMO, and it doesn't need to be as large as them. They both have specific config to do their jobs, and Sepolia is probably the most specialised with its permissioned validator set... 

Do we need something like a long running closed validator set testnet that we can break outside of our devnets? It seems like this would be only useful during upgrade, so maybe its more like a devnet that exhibits the same properties as Sepolia, and we can upgrade that, and then one that is similar in all aspects to holesky (deposit contract, anything else) and upgrade that then let it run for a few days, then kill them...

I guess this was previously shadow forks, but it sounded like shadow forks weren't an option maybe for these pre-prod networks...

Re. dates, we've agreed the 30 day release window prior to mainnet, and it sounds like portal network has a 1st may date? also L2 has expressed a desire for more blobs by may, but that would mean:

 - mainnet date prior to May 1
 - mainnet release prior to 1 April (for that 30 day window)
 - 3 days for a release for some clients, so 27 march start at very latest?
 - time for whatever testing we need to get confidence for a mainnet release prior to that

so now it's 13 march, and we need to probably be cutting releases by 27 march... and most of the solutions for testing take us longer than we would hit that date... Is there anything that could give us confidence before we would need to start those releases or do we call 1 may unrealistic now?

Hey! From Rocket Pool's perspective (and I suspect other protocols) - we prefer plan A. 

**Plan A** - means we can redeploy our testnet and get on with our lives 😂 
**Plan B** - our testnet is our staging environment, it is long lived, and we engage our community around it, so we have a good participation. Using Plan B we would have to resetup all the infra and reengage the community.
**Plan C** - we would have to redeploy the testnet because the state would be inconsistent across EL/CL, so this is essentially the same as Plan A but less long lived
**Plan D** - seems like major effort for you guys and it wouldn't gain much from our perspective

Re PeerDAS EIP change (also mentioned by @ralexstokes & @dapplion above)

> It sounds like what we actually have in sepolia and holesky (or whatever its replaced with maybe) is 2 pre-production deployments

yeah, that's a great way to put it.

I echo the sentiment that: 
- Testnet being treated as a relatively long-lived staging environment by many.
- Many end users / communities are actively engaging in that staging testnet ruling out very short-lived ones.
- Still keeping a decent window prior to mainnet release no matter what (30+ days)

Which means option D or option A would be the most practical.

Hi Tim, I want to take the discussions for https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9460 async, because I currently do not have a strong opinion here and it is about a super niche point. I might raise this point again in a later ACD-E. Could you remove this from the agenda? Thanks 😄 👍

Grandine prefers option A. However, I strongly suggest making one of these networks a regular non-finality network. We must include long non-finality in the regular testing workflow before releasing mainnet hardfork. One large testnet should try to replicate mainnet stability we had so far. Second network should be dedicated for long non-finality periods. Once we have this in place we should enhance the second network with more exotic scenarios such as mass slashing etc.

Looks like (at least according to the comments above) that the majority of the community would like to go with option A. - start a new testnet.  We can ratify that on the call, but in the meantime we have a proposition for this new testnet.

We would like to propose a few [options](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/hoodi) for the genesis validator set. 

Proposed name: Hoodi (metro station in Bangalore) 
Estimated date for launch: By end of March 2025.
Mascot: Peacock in a hoodie.

In terms of the path forward, also in favor of A or B. In particular I think adding more complex corner cases (D) is likely to risk bugs in future, and I'd rather spend more effort now to reduce risks.
